history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that delegation of authority to any Officers-in-Charge is visible in the delegation of authority portal, and define and codify the delegation of authority for administrative decisions regarding the management of resources, including human resources, for all drawdown and liquidation activities after the Security Council mandate of a mission has ended.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that in the revised ST/SGB/2019/2/Rev.1, which is in the final review stage, the policy has been modified to indicate that when an officer-in-charge arrangement is put in place to assume the function held by an official whose post has become vacant, the authorities are to be delegated to the officer-in-charge in the online portal. The delegation of authority portal had already been enhanced to allow the delegation “in the capacity of officer- in-charge” as part of the latest portal enhancements implemented in September 2021. This functionality is already in use, and the Administration considers this part of the recommendation as closed. The revised ST/SGB also includes a new section on the exercise of temporary delegated authority at the closure of operations of an entity, which clarifies the delegation holder in such scenarios. The Administration will consider this recommendation closed when the revised ST/SGB is published.
history.board_assessment: The delegation of authority portal has been enhanced but the ST/SGB has not been revised. The Board considers this recommendation as under implementation.

history.administration_response: The Administration has taken action to implement this recommendation by including in Secretary-General’s bulletin ST/SGB/2019/2/Rev.1, which is under the final review stage: (a) a new disposition stating that, in the case that an officer-in- charge arrangement is put in place to assume the function held by an official whose post has become vacant, the authorities will be delegated to the officer- in-charge in the online portal until the successor or the acting officer is appointed (for heads of entities, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division has already implemented this provision in the delegation of authority portal); and (b) a new section clarifying the exercise of temporary delegated authority at the closure of operations of an entity. The Administration will request the closure of this recommendation as soon as the revised bulletin is published, in 2025.
history.board_assessment: Once the revised Secretary-General’s bulletin is published, the recommendation will be considered implemented.

history.sg_progress: The Administration has put in place interim policy arrangements, such as the modalities for delegating authority to an officer-in-charge and regarding the exercise of delegated authority at the start-up and closure of a mission. The recommendation will be fully implemented following publication of the revised Secretary-General’s bulletin on delegation of authority in the administration of the Staff Regulations and Rules and the Financial Regulations and Rules (ST/SGB/2019/2), which codifies these interim arrangements in a single policy document. The revised Secretary- General’s bulletin and instrument are in the final review stage and are expected to be published in 2025. An enhanced delegation of authority portal will be rolled out alongside the revised policy. Implementation of this recommendation was delayed owing to resource constraints and competing priorities. history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that the delegation of authority to any Officers-in- Charge is visible in the delegation of authority portal, and define and codify the delegation of authority for administrative decisions regarding the management of resources, including human resources, for all drawdown and liquidation activities after the Security Council mandate of a mission has ended.
history.administration_response: The Administration reiterates that it has successfully operationalized the modalities for delegating authority to officers-in-charge through the delegation of authority portal and codified the delegation of authority during the recent closure of missions. This framework was effectively applied during the closure of MINUSMA, for example, demonstrating the robustness and adequacy of the modalities put in place based on the recommendation. Accordingly, the Administration requests the closure of the recommendation. The Board is respectfully invited to review the evidence that has been provided, taken from the delegation of authority portal in the case of MINUSMA.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the implementation of the delegation of authority portal regarding officers-in-charge and considers the recommendation to be implemented.
